chapter: Big bands, small groups and studio work
title: Leaving Cab for Raymond Scott's CBS staff

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Well let's see. At this point why don't we talk about once you left Cab, which was.
According to Chalton, let's see, August 1942.
And it says, 'Briefly with Raymond Scott from September '42 and remained on CBS staff until August 1943.' Let's talk about that period.
Well that was a great experience. See I was one of the first black drummers to be on staff at CBS. There was four of us altogether.

Billy Taylor and George Johnson, saxophone, four of us. Well there's where you gained an awful lot of experience, there with Raymond, because we were doing the Perry Como show at that time, he was doing a sustaining program, three to 3:15 in the afternoon, Perry Como, then Dorothy Collins. Then we would Baron, what was his name, he was another leader up there that had a band, and you used to free lance up there with different conductors. Play all different styles of music. Raymond, of course, as you know was a superb musician, and he'd have any sort of things, any sort of difficult numbers he'd bring out for you to play. At one time there we had a big band with two drummers--Johnny Blowers and me, two bass players and two guitars in a big band. And then sometimes we used to do a Good Morning Blues program which was early in the morning, that consist of Mel Powell piano, Emmett Barry, George Johnson clarinet and

saxophone, Billy Taylor bass and me, and Raymond, we used to play the blues, Good Morning Blues program, then sometimes we'd get out of that idiom, start playing up tempo things, 'After You've Gone' and things like that. And it called for an awful lot of control, especially that time in the morning, eight o'clock in the morning you know to get those breakneck tempos.
Most guys are lucky if they can play anything.
Oh yeah, sure, at that time. At that time in the morning. But there's where I got a lot of experience. Right there at CBS.
